points: Say the six types cover the options most homeowners are quoted: gas tank, electric tank, heat pump, gas tankless, electric tankless and gas power vent.

outline.h2: 1. Gas tank water heater: best for most homes with gas service
points: Say what it does well: it is the most common and most affordable mid-range option, with fast recovery times [6].
Give pricing: unit $800 to $2,850, labor $500 to $1,200, total installed $1,300 to $4,050, average about $2,000 [6].
Give the tank-size effect: a 50 gallon gas unit typically runs $1,100 to $3,200 installed and is the most common replacement [6].
Pros: lower upfront cost, simpler install, minimal maintenance [8][7].
Cons: standby heat loss means higher running costs than tankless, and the lifespan is shorter at about 8 to 12 years [8][7].
Who should skip it: homes without gas service, or homeowners who want endless hot water.

outline.h2: 2. Electric tank water heater: best for the lowest upfront price
points: Pricing: unit $700 to $1,800, labor $500 to $1,200, total installed $1,200 to $3,000, average about $1,500 [6].
What it does well: it is cheap to install [9].
Con: a standard electric resistance tank has higher operating costs than a heat pump unit [9].
Tell readers an electric replacement is a good moment to compare a heat pump model before defaulting to another tank [9].
Who should skip it: homeowners planning to stay long enough for energy savings to matter.

outline.h2: 3. Heat pump water heater: best for lower energy bills
points: Explain that it uses electricity to move heat from the surrounding air into the tank instead of making heat directly [9].
Pricing: unit $1,200 to $4,800, labor $800 to $1,500, total installed $2,000 to $6,300, average about $3,000 [6]. Another source lists $2,000 to $4,600 [8].
Pro: highest long-term energy savings, using roughly a third the energy of a standard electric tank [6][9]. Lifespan of 12 to 15 years with proper maintenance [2].

Con and who should skip it: it needs enough airflow, typically 700 to 1,000 cubic feet of space or ducting and louvered doors, and it cools and adds some noise to its room, so a small closet may not work [6][9].
Tell readers to check current rebate and incentive availability with their utility before buying, because terms change [6][10].

outline.h2: 4. Gas tankless water heater: best for long life and endless hot water
points: Explain that it heats water on demand and avoids standby heat loss [1][7].
Pricing: unit $1,800 to $2,750, labor $1,500 to $3,500, total installed $3,300 to $6,250, average about $4,250, roughly 2 to 3 times a standard tank [6].
Pro: a 15 to 20 year lifespan can offset the premium over time [6][8].
Cons: it may need venting and gas-line upgrades, must be sized for your simultaneous hot water use, and a limited flow rate can struggle at peak use [9][7][8].
Who should skip it: homeowners who want the lowest upfront cost or who plan to move soon.

outline.h2: 5. Electric tankless water heater: best for on-demand hot water with a strong electrical setup
points: Pricing: unit $800 to $1,500, labor $300 to $1,200, total installed $1,100 to $2,700, average about $1,900 [6].
What it does well: on-demand hot water and a lower installed price than gas tankless [6][1].
Con: the heating elements draw substantial instantaneous power, so have a licensed electrician or plumber confirm your electrical requirements first [9][8].
Con: the limited flow rate can struggle during peak use [8].
Who should skip it: homes with a busy hot water schedule or limited electrical service.

outline.h2: 6. Gas power vent water heater: best for homes where venting needs more work
points: Pricing: unit $1,750 to $3,250, labor $1,500 to $2,750, total installed $3,250 to $6,000, average about $4,500 [6].
Point out that labor is the larger share of this type's cost, which is why it sits near gas tankless in price [6].
Tell readers to ask the plumber why this type fits their venting situation before agreeing to it [7].
Who should skip it: homeowners with a straightforward gas tank swap, where a standard gas tank is the lower-priced match [6].

outline.h2: How to choose the right water heater replacement
points: Match tank size to household size, since moving from a 40 to a 75 gallon tank can more than double replacement cost and oversizing can add 15 to 20% to water heating costs [6].
Use the household guide: 30 gallons for 1 to 2 people, 40 gallons for 1 to 4, 50 gallons for 3 to 5, 75 gallons for 4 to 6 [6].
Know the signs it's time: strange noises, leaks, inconsistent hot water, rust, pooling water, a leaking relief valve, or an age of 8 to 12 years for a tank [1][9].
Replace on your schedule, because waiting for a failure can add an emergency premium [7].

h3.title: What a fair quote includes
points: The unit and its capacity, labor for removal and installation, the permit and inspection where required, disposal of the old unit and any code upgrades [7].
Compare installed totals, not store prices for the unit alone [7].

h3.title: Extra costs to ask about
points: An expansion tank, new venting, gas-line resizing, electrical work, and repair of water or sediment damage [7].
Ask the plumber to list any that apply before work starts, since a surprise on the invoice often means the quote was incomplete [7].

h3.title: Ways to lower the cost
points: Right-size the unit, ask about manufacturer or utility rebates, and replace before the old unit fails [7].
Hard water can shorten a heater's life, so ask about a water softener if you have it [1][7].

blocks.text: If your water heater leaks, rumbles or runs out of hot water, you probably want a clear number for what a replacement will cost.

In this guide, we walk you through six common water heater types, each with its installed price range and who it suits best. As you can see, your fuel, your household size and your space all affect which type fits, so we finish with a simple way to match them.

sections.h2: How we picked these 6 water heater replacements

blocks.text: We picked the six water heater types that most homeowners are quoted when a heater needs replacing. Here's how we built the list and how you can read the prices that follow.

items: A gas tank water heater is the most common option for homes with gas service.
An electric tank water heater is the simplest choice for homes without gas.
A heat pump (hybrid) water heater moves heat from the surrounding air into the tank.
A gas tankless water heater heats water on demand using a gas line.
An electric tankless water heater heats water on demand using electricity.
A gas power vent water heater uses a fan to push exhaust out through a vent.

blocks.text: Every price in this guide is a total installed cost, which means the unit plus labor. Our main source is the [2026 dataset from Paul Bunyan Plumbing](https://paulbunyanplumbing.com/blog/average-water-heater-replacement-cost), and we added other pages where they filled in a gap.

You may notice that ranges differ from page to page. That happens because [price depends on unit type, tank size, fuel source and local labor rates](https://paulbunyanplumbing.com/blog/average-water-heater-replacement-cost), and [any plumbing or electrical upgrades a retrofit needs can add to the total](https://homeguide.com/costs/water-heater-installation-cost).

You can use those ranges as a planning guide. They come from national or other-city sources, so an Austin quote can differ, and a written quote is the best way to confirm your real number. If you're curious how we build ours, here's [how we price our work](https://brightwaterplumbing.example/pricing).
We score each type on the same four points so you can compare them side by side:

items: We look at installed cost, which comes from the unit and labor together.
We look at expected lifespan, since a longer-lasting heater can offset a higher price over time.
We look at install needs, such as venting, gas lines or electrical work.

sections.h2: 1. Gas tank water heater: best for most homes with gas service

blocks.text: A gas tank water heater is the most common and most affordable mid-range option, and it recovers quickly after you use up the hot water, according to [Paul Bunyan Plumbing's 2026 data](https://paulbunyanplumbing.com/blog/average-water-heater-replacement-cost). If your home has natural gas service, this is usually where we start the conversation.

The unit itself runs $800 to $2,850 and labor adds $500 to $1,200, which puts the total installed cost at $1,300 to $4,050, with an average near $2,000, as [that same dataset](https://paulbunyanplumbing.com/blog/average-water-heater-replacement-cost) shows.

Tank size moves the price too, since a 50 gallon gas unit typically runs $1,100 to $3,200 fully installed and is the [most common replacement](https://paulbunyanplumbing.com/blog/average-water-heater-replacement-cost). That makes it a handy number to keep in mind when you compare quotes for [water heater replacement and installation](https://brightwaterplumbing.example/services/water-heaters).
Here's what a gas tank does well:

items: It has a lower upfront cost than tankless and heat pump models, which helps if you need a new heater soon.
The install is simpler because tank units need [fewer modifications and less labor](https://homeguide.com/costs/water-heater-installation-cost) than other types.
Maintenance stays minimal, so you won't have much to keep up with after the install.

blocks.text: Here's what to weigh against those strengths:

items: The tank keeps water hot all day, which causes [standby heat loss](https://homeguide.com/costs/water-heater-installation-cost) and means higher running costs than a tankless unit.

blocks.text: This type isn't the right match if your home doesn't have gas service or if you want endless hot water, because a tank can run out when several people use hot water back to back.

sections.h2: 2. Electric tank water heater: best for the lowest upfront price

blocks.text: An electric tank is a low-priced way to get hot water back in your home. [Paul Bunyan Plumbing's 2026 cost data](https://paulbunyanplumbing.com/blog/average-water-heater-replacement-cost) puts the unit at $700 to $1,800 and labor at $500 to $1,200, for a total installed cost of $1,200 to $3,000.

The average in that same dataset is about $1,500, so most homeowners land near the middle of the range. These are national figures, so a written quote from us is the best way to confirm what you'd pay in Austin.
For a homeowner who needs hot water soon, three things stand out:

items: The installed price is lower than heat pump, gas tankless or power vent models, which helps if your budget is tight.
A standard electric resistance tank has higher operating costs than a heat pump unit, so your monthly bills can run higher over time.

blocks.text: If you're replacing an electric heater, this is a good moment to compare a heat pump model before you default to another tank. [A heat pump unit](https://servhom.com/guides/nyc-water-heater-replacement-cost) uses electricity to move heat from the surrounding air into the tank, which makes for a very different operating-cost picture, and we cover that type in the next section.

You may want to skip an electric tank if you plan to stay in your home long enough for energy savings to matter. In that case, the higher running cost can add up, and a more efficient type may cost you less over the years.

sections.h2: 3. Heat pump water heater: best for lower energy bills

blocks.text: A heat pump water heater is an electric water heater that uses electricity to [move heat from the surrounding air into the tank](https://servhom.com/guides/nyc-water-heater-replacement-cost) instead of making heat directly, which is why its operating costs look so different from a standard electric tank.

One source puts the unit at [$1,200 to $4,800 and labor at $800 to $1,500](https://paulbunyanplumbing.com/blog/average-water-heater-replacement-cost), for a total installed cost of $2,000 to $6,300 and an average near $3,000.
Here's why it works for many homes, and what you should weigh before you choose one:

items: It offers the highest long-term energy savings, using [roughly a third the energy of a standard electric tank](https://servhom.com/guides/nyc-water-heater-replacement-cost), according to a New York City guide from ServHom.
With proper maintenance, one plumbing company says these units typically [last 12 to 15 years](https://www.callmattioni.com/blog/t-water-heater-cost).
It needs enough airflow, which is typically [700 to 1,000 cubic feet of space](https://paulbunyanplumbing.com/blog/average-water-heater-replacement-cost) or proper ducting and louvered doors.
It cools and adds some noise to the room it sits in, so [a small enclosed closet is not always a good fit](https://servhom.com/guides/nyc-water-heater-replacement-cost).

blocks.text: You may want to skip this type if your heater lives in a tight closet with little air around it, so ask your plumber whether your space is suitable before you commit.

Incentives for heat pump units have shifted recently. The [federal tax credit for efficient water heaters covered only improvements made through December 31, 2025](https://abendplumbingandheating.com/expert-tips/water-heater-replacement-cost-in-maryland-tank-tankless-and-permit-fees), and the [national dataset we use advises checking current rebate availability](https://paulbunyanplumbing.com/blog/average-water-heater-replacement-cost) because terms may change.
Honestly, none of these sources cover Austin utility rebates, so ask your utility what it offers today before you buy, and we're happy to help you plan around it.

sections.h2: 4. Gas tankless water heater: best for long life and endless hot water

blocks.text: A gas tankless water heater heats water only when you open a tap, so it has no tank of hot water sitting around losing heat. This is why [tankless units avoid standby heat loss](https://homeguide.com/costs/water-heater-installation-cost) and can give you a steady supply of hot water on demand.

For pricing, [Paul Bunyan Plumbing's 2026 data](https://paulbunyanplumbing.com/blog/average-water-heater-replacement-cost) puts the unit at $1,800 to $2,750 and labor at $1,500 to $3,500. The total installed cost runs $3,300 to $6,250, with an average near $4,250, which is roughly 2 to 3 times the cost of a standard tank.
Here's why it works for some homes, and what you should weigh before you choose one:

items: It may need venting and gas-line upgrades, and [HomeGuide notes that installation is more complex](https://homeguide.com/costs/water-heater-installation-cost) than for a tank.

It must be sized for your simultaneous hot water use, and [one New York guide says to confirm sizing](https://servhom.com/guides/nyc-water-heater-replacement-cost) against how much hot water your home runs at once.
A limited flow rate can [struggle to keep up during peak use](https://homeguide.com/costs/water-heater-installation-cost), which is when several taps run at the same time.

blocks.text: You may want to skip this type if you want the lowest upfront cost or plan to move soon, because the savings take years to add up.
If you're weighing this type, ask your plumber how a tankless unit would handle your home's peak hot water use.

sections.h2: 5. Electric tankless water heater: best for on-demand hot water with a strong electrical setup

blocks.text: An electric tankless unit heats water only when you open a tap, so you get on-demand hot water without a storage tank. Paul Bunyan Plumbing's 2026 data puts the [unit cost at $800 to $1,500 and labor at $300 to $1,200](https://paulbunyanplumbing.com/blog/average-water-heater-replacement-cost), for a total installed cost of $1,100 to $2,700 and an average near $1,900.
In that same dataset, gas tankless units average about $4,250 installed, so the electric type has the lower installed price.
Here's what you should weigh before you choose one:

items: The heating elements draw substantial instantaneous power, so a licensed electrician or plumber should [confirm the unit's electrical requirements](https://servhom.com/guides/nyc-water-heater-replacement-cost) against your home's service before you buy.

HomeGuide lists [upgrades to gas lines, electrical wiring or ventilation](https://homeguide.com/costs/water-heater-installation-cost) as part of the more complex installation that tankless units can need.
A [restricted flow rate](https://homeguide.com/costs/water-heater-installation-cost) may struggle to provide enough hot water during peak use, such as when two showers run at once.

blocks.text: You may want to skip this type if your home has a busy hot water schedule or limited electrical service. Honestly, asking a licensed pro to confirm your electrical requirements before you buy can spare you a surprise on the invoice.
Does your family tend to run several hot water fixtures at the same time? If so, ask your plumber to size the unit for that demand before you agree to a quote.

sections.h2: 6. Gas power vent water heater: best for homes where venting needs more work

blocks.text: According to [Paul Bunyan Plumbing's 2026 data](https://paulbunyanplumbing.com/blog/average-water-heater-replacement-cost), the unit costs $1,750 to $3,250, and labor adds $1,500 to $2,750.
That brings the total installed cost to $3,250 to $6,000, with an average of about $4,500.
Here's what you should do before you agree to this type:

items: Ask your plumber to explain why a power vent unit fits your venting situation.
Ask whether a standard gas tank could use your existing vent instead.

Ask for an itemized quote that lists venting work as its own line, since [a complete quote should list each part of the job](https://www.newyorkplumbingdirectory.com/resources/water-heater-replacement-cost-new-york).

blocks.text: Once your plumber has seen where your heater sits and how it vents today, these questions are much easier to answer. Does your current vent have room for a standard tank, or does your space call for something different?

Honestly, you may want to skip this type if you have a straightforward gas tank swap. In that case, a standard gas tank is the lower-priced match, with [total installed costs of $1,300 to $4,050](https://paulbunyanplumbing.com/blog/average-water-heater-replacement-cost) and an average near $2,000.

sections.h2: How to choose the right water heater replacement

blocks.text: To pick a water heater, you match tank size to your household, fuel type to your home, and price to your budget. Here's how we'd walk through it with you.

Start with size. According to [Paul Bunyan Plumbing's 2026 data](https://paulbunyanplumbing.com/blog/average-water-heater-replacement-cost), moving from a 40 gallon tank to a 75 gallon tank can more than double your total replacement cost, and oversizing can add 15 to 20% to your water heating costs because the tank keeps heating water your household never uses.
For a tank-style heater, [this household guide](https://paulbunyanplumbing.com/blog/average-water-heater-replacement-cost) is a good starting point:

items: 30 gallons suits a household of 1 to 2 people.
40 gallons suits a household of 1 to 4 people.
50 gallons suits a household of 3 to 5 people.
75 gallons suits a household of 4 to 6 people.

blocks.text: [ServHom](https://servhom.com/guides/nyc-water-heater-replacement-cost) adds rust, pooling water and a leaking relief valve to the list of warning signs.

Luckily, the best time to replace is before the heater fails, and [New York Plumbing Directory](https://www.newyorkplumbingdirectory.com/resources/water-heater-replacement-cost-new-york) notes that replacing on your own schedule helps you avoid paying an emergency premium. If you're already dealing with a leak, we offer [emergency plumbing help](https://brightwaterplumbing.example/services/emergency), and our [water heater guide](https://brightwaterplumbing.example/blog/water-heater-guide) can help you plan ahead.
What a fair quote includes

A complete quote should list each part of the job, according to [New York Plumbing Directory](https://www.newyorkplumbingdirectory.com/resources/water-heater-replacement-cost-new-york). Here's what to look for:

items: The water heater unit and its capacity.
Labor for removing the old unit and installing the new one.
The permit and inspection where required.
Disposal of the old unit.
Any code upgrades needed to bring the install current.

blocks.text: Compare installed totals instead of store prices for the unit alone, because the same source points out that labor, permits, hauling and code upgrades are where quotes differ.
Extra costs to ask about

Some line items can turn a low quote into a higher final bill, as [New York Plumbing Directory](https://www.newyorkplumbingdirectory.com/resources/water-heater-replacement-cost-new-york) explains. Ask whether any of these apply to your home:

items: An expansion tank.
New venting for the unit.
Gas-line resizing for a higher-demand heater.
Electrical work for an electric or hybrid unit.
Repair of water or sediment damage from the old unit.

blocks.text: Ask your plumber to list any that apply before work starts, since a surprise on the invoice often means the quote was incomplete.
Ways to lower the cost

items: Right-size the unit to your household so you aren't paying to heat water you never use.

Ask your plumber about manufacturer or utility rebates, which [New York Plumbing Directory](https://www.newyorkplumbingdirectory.com/resources/water-heater-replacement-cost-new-york) lists as a way to save.
Replace the old unit before it fails so you avoid an emergency premium.

blocks.text: Hard water can also shorten a heater's life, so ask about a water softener if you have hard water, as [Benjamin Franklin Plumbing](https://www.benjaminfranklinplumbing.com/league-city/blog/2024/december/how-much-is-a-water-heater-replacement-costs-and-considerations/) suggests.
